questions.question: What record does Walt Disney hold as a film producer according to the article?
options: Most Academy Awards won and nominations by an individual
Most Golden Globe Awards won by an individual
Most Emmy Awards won by an individual
Most films included in the National Film Registry
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that as a film producer, Disney holds the record for most Academy Awards won (22) and nominations (59) by an individual.
Incorrect. The article mentions he received two Golden Globe Special Achievement Awards, but does not say he holds the record for most Golden Globe wins.
Incorrect. The article notes he received an Emmy Award, but does not state he holds the record for most Emmy wins.
Incorrect. While several of his films are in the National Film Registry, the article does not say he holds the record for most films included.

questions.question: Where was Walt Disney born and raised largely?
options: Born in Chicago and raised largely in Missouri
Born in Missouri and raised largely in Chicago
Born in Kansas City and raised largely in Marceline
Born in California and raised largely in Hollywood
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Disney was born in Chicago in 1901 and raised largely in Missouri.
Incorrect. The article states the opposite: born in Chicago, raised largely in Missouri.
Incorrect. Kansas City and Marceline are places he lived in Missouri, but he was born in Chicago.
Incorrect. He moved to California in the early 1920s, but was not born or raised there.

questions.question: Which character did Walt Disney develop with Ub Iwerks in 1928?
options: Mickey Mouse
Oswald the Lucky Rabbit
Pinocchio
Snow White
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that with Ub Iwerks, Disney developed Mickey Mouse in 1928, his first highly popular success.
Incorrect. Oswald the Lucky Rabbit was created earlier, in 1927, after Mintz requested new material for Universal Pictures.
Incorrect. Pinocchio is a feature film released in 1940, not a character developed with Iwerks in 1928.
Incorrect. Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs is a feature film released in 1937.

questions.question: What did Walt Disney do in the 1950s regarding theme parks?
options: He opened Disneyland in Anaheim, California in July 1955
He opened Disney World in Florida
He opened EPCOT as a completed city
He closed all theme park operations
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that in the 1950s, Disney expanded into the theme park industry and opened Disneyland in Anaheim, California in July 1955.
Incorrect. Disney World development began in 1965, after Disney's death, and was not opened in the 1950s.
Incorrect. EPCOT was planned as a new type of city but was never completed before Disney's death in 1966.
Incorrect. The article describes expansion into theme parks, not closure.

questions.question: How did Walt Disney attempt to serve in World War I?
options: He forged his birth certificate to join the Red Cross as an ambulance driver
He successfully enlisted in the United States Army
He fought on the Western Front in France
He served as a cartoonist for Stars and Stripes only
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Disney was rejected by the Army as too young, then forged his birth certificate to join the Red Cross in September 1918 as an ambulance driver.
Incorrect. The article says he was rejected by the United States Army as too young.
Incorrect. He was shipped to France but arrived in November 1918, after the armistice, so he did not fight on the Western Front.
Incorrect. While some of his work was published in Stars and Stripes, his primary service was as a Red Cross ambulance driver.

questions.question: What happened when Walt Disney sought a larger budget for the Oswald series in February 1928?
options: Mintz refused and Disney lost most of his animation staff
Mintz agreed and increased the budget
Universal immediately fired Mintz and gave Disney full rights
Disney accepted the reductions and kept all his staff
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Mintz refused the larger budget after Disney traveled to New York, and Disney lost most of his animation staff except Iwerks.
Incorrect. The article says Mintz refused the larger budget, not that he agreed.
Incorrect. Carl Laemmle later terminated Mintz's contract, but this was after Disney had already lost his staff and declined the ultimatum.
Incorrect. Disney declined Mintz's ultimatum and lost most of his staff.

questions.question: Which of the following is described as a technical development introduced by Disney as his studio grew?
options: Synchronized sound and full-color three-strip Technicolor
Computer-generated imagery
3D animation
Virtual reality filmmaking
answer_explanations: Correct. The article lists synchronized sound, full-color three-strip Technicolor, animated feature films, and technical developments in cameras as developments Disney introduced.
Incorrect. Computer-generated imagery is not mentioned in the article.
Incorrect. 3D animation is not mentioned in the article.
Incorrect. Virtual reality filmmaking is not mentioned in the article.

questions.question: What was Walt Disney's private personality like according to the article?
options: Shy, self-deprecating, and insecure
Warm and outgoing in all settings
Racist and antisemitic
Indifferent to those he worked with
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Disney was shy, self-deprecating, and insecure in private but adopted a warm and outgoing public persona.
Incorrect. The warm and outgoing persona was his public persona, not his private personality.
Incorrect. The article mentions accusations of racism and antisemitism but says they were contradicted by many who knew him.
Incorrect. The article says he had high standards and high expectations of those with whom he worked.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the Experimental Prototype Community of Tomorrow (EPCOT)?
options: It was to be the heart of Disney World, a new type of city
It was a television program about space exploration
It was a live-action film released in 1964
It was a Red Cross ambulance decoration project
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Disney World's heart was to be EPCOT, described as a new type of city.
Incorrect. EPCOT was not a television program; the article mentions television programs like Walt Disney's Disneyland and The Mickey Mouse Club separately.
Incorrect. Mary Poppins (1964) was the live-action film mentioned, not EPCOT.
Incorrect. Drawing cartoons on ambulances was his Red Cross activity in France, unrelated to EPCOT.

questions.question: Which of the following films is listed in the article as receiving five Academy Awards?
options: Mary Poppins
Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
Fantasia
Dumbo
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states Mary Poppins (1964) received five Academy Awards.
Incorrect. Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937) is listed as furthering animated film but not as receiving five Academy Awards.
Incorrect. Fantasia (1940) is listed among the features that furthered animated film, not as receiving five Academy Awards.
Incorrect. Dumbo (1941) is listed among the features that furthered animated film, not as receiving five Academy Awards.
